ideas.children_he: קָרְבַּן אָשָׁם הֻקְרַב לְפִי כְּלָלִים קְבוּעִים, וְחֲלָקִים מִמֶּנּוּ נִתְּנוּ לַכֹּהֲנִים.
ideas.children_en: The guilt offering followed set rules, and parts of it were given to the priests.

ideas.children_he: הַכֹּהֲנִים קִבְּלוּ חֲלָקִים מִסֻּגֵּי קָרְבָּנוֹת שׁוֹנִים כְּחֵלֶק מֵעֲבוֹדָתָם.
ideas.children_en: The priests received parts of different offerings as part of their service.

ideas.children_he: מִי שֶׁהֵבִיא קָרְבַּן תּוֹדָה הֵבִיא גַּם לֶחֶם. אֶת בְּשַׂר הַקָּרְבָּן אָכְלוּ בְּאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם.
ideas.children_en: Someone bringing a thanksgiving offering also brought bread. The meat was eaten that same day.

ideas.children_he: בְּקָרְבַּן נֶדֶר אוֹ נְדָבָה יָכְלוּ לֶאֱכֹל גַּם לְמָחֳרָת. אֶת הַנּוֹתָר אַחַר כָּךְ הָיוּ צְרִיכִים לִשְׂרֹף.
ideas.children_en: An offering made to fulfill a vow or as a free gift could also be eaten the next day. Anything left after that had to be burned.

ideas.children_he: בְּשַׂר קָרְבָּן שֶׁנִּטְמָא לֹא הָיָה מֻתָּר לֶאֱכֹל. הַתּוֹרָה דָּרְשָׁה לִשְׁמֹר עַל טָהֳרַת הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת.
ideas.children_en: Offering meat that became ritually impure could not be eaten. The Torah required care to keep offerings ritually pure.

ideas.children_he: הַתּוֹרָה אָסְרָה לֶאֱכֹל דָּם וְחֵלֶב מְסֻיָּם שֶׁמְּיֹעָד לַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
ideas.children_en: The Torah forbade eating blood and certain fat that was meant for the altar.

ideas.children_he: מִי שֶׁהֵבִיא קָרְבַּן שְׁלָמִים הֵבִיא בְּעַצְמוֹ אֶת הַחֲלָקִים הַמְּיֹעָדִים לַכֹּהֲנִים וְלַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
ideas.children_en: The person bringing a peace offering personally brought the parts meant for the priests and the altar.

ideas.children_he: חֵלֶק מֵהַקָּרְבָּן נִשְׂרַף עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, וְהֶחָזֶה וְשׁוֹק הַיָּמִין נִתְּנוּ לַכֹּהֲנִים.
ideas.children_en: Part of the offering was burned on the altar. The breast and right thigh were given to the priests.

ideas.children_he: הַתּוֹרָה קָבְעָה אֵילוּ חֲלָקִים מִן הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת שַׁיָּכִים לַכֹּהֲנִים.
ideas.children_en: The Torah set out which parts of the offerings belonged to the priests.

ideas.children_he: בְּסוֹף הַפֶּרֶק מְסַכְּמִים אֶת סֻגֵּי הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת וְאֶת הַכְּלָלִים שֶׁנִּתְּנוּ בְּהַר סִינַי.
ideas.children_en: The chapter ends by reviewing the kinds of offerings and the rules given at Mount Sinai.
